skill.name: tester
skill.description: Minimal tester skill for confirming that an AI skill loads and responds.
skill.summary: Provides a small prompt for skill activation smoke tests.
skill.author: 0xSero

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported no suspicious patterns in the single prompt-only SKILL.md file. I found no evidence of prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, executable code, network activity, or filesystem access.

content.user_title: Test Prompt Workflows With a Minimal Skill
content.value_statement: Teams need a small skill for checking that marketplace installation and invocation work. This skill provides a minimal tester prompt for validating basic AI skill wiring.
actual_capabilities: Loads a skill named tester with a short description.
Provides a minimal test prompt for activation checks.
Uses automatic model selection through its metadata.
Requires no scripts, assets, or runtime setup.
Serves as a simple baseline for marketplace smoke tests.
limitations: It does not include a detailed testing methodology.
It does not run automated tests or inspect repositories.
It does not define specialized output formats.
It should be extended before use in production workflows.

use_cases.title: Marketplace Smoke Testing
use_cases.description: Confirm that a skill package can be discovered, loaded, and invoked in a marketplace review flow.

use_cases.title: Agent Setup Checks
use_cases.description: Verify that Claude, Codex, or Claude Code can access a newly installed skill before adding complex instructions.

use_cases.title: Starter Skill Template
use_cases.description: Use the small prompt and metadata as a starting point for a more specific custom skill.

prompt_templates.title: Confirm Activation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tester skill and confirm whether it activated. Summarize the skill name and the prompt context you received.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Smoke Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tester skill to perform a smoke test. Report whether the skill loaded, whether metadata was available, and whether any setup step was required.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Tool Support
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tester skill as a baseline. Compare how it behaves in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code, and note any visible differences.

prompt_templates.title: Audit as a Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tester skill as a template baseline. Identify which fields need stronger instructions before it can support a real testing workflow.

output_examples.input: Use tester to confirm skill loading.
output_examples.output: The tester skill loaded successfully. It contains a short test prompt and does not require setup steps.

output_examples.input: Review tester as a starting point for a custom skill.
output: The skill is suitable as a minimal activation check.
Add task-specific instructions before using it for real test planning.
No scripts, network calls, or external files are included.

best_practices: Use this skill for smoke tests before installing larger skills.
Pair it with a clear validation request because the prompt is minimal.
Replace the placeholder prompt before using it for domain work.
anti_patterns: Do not expect it to execute a test suite.
Do not use it as a security audit skill.
Do not publish it as a full workflow without adding instructions.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It provides a minimal tester prompt for confirming that a skill can load and respond.

faq.question: Does it run automated tests?
faq.answer: No. It does not execute test suites, inspect files, or call external tools.

faq.question: Is it useful for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It is suitable for basic activation checks across supported AI tools.

faq.question: Can I use it as a template?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it as a small starting point, then add specific instructions for your workflow.

faq.question: Does it require setup?
faq.answer: No. The skill contains only metadata and a short prompt.

faq.question: Is it ready for production testing workflows?
faq.answer: No. It needs detailed testing goals, expected outputs, and validation steps first.
